entries.sanskrit:
षड्विंशे विस्मितान् गोपान् कृष्णस्याद्भुत-कर्मभिः ।

नन्दो गर्गोक्तिम् आश्राव्य तद्-ऐश्वर्यम् अवर्णयत् ॥

समभ्येत्य नन्दम् अभिगम्य ॥१॥
word_for_word: having caused Garga’s words to be heard
entries.literal_english: In the Twenty-sixth Chapter, Nanda, having approached the cowherd men astonished by Kṛṣṇa’s amazing deeds, had Garga’s words heard and described Kṛṣṇa’s opulence.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: यद् ऊचुः, तद् आह---बालकस्येति । यद् यस्माद् अद्भुतानि कर्माणि, तस्माद् ग्राम्येषु गोपालेषु कथं जन्मार्हति ? आत्म-जुगुप्सितम् आत्मानर्हम् ॥२॥
entries.literal_english: They said: “Because this boy performs amazing deeds, how could He have been born among rustic cowherds? Such a birth seems unworthy of the Self.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: अद्भुतानि कर्माण्य् आहुह्---यः सप्त-हायन इति । कथं बिभ्रत् स्थितः ? इति । पुष्करं पद्मं गज-राण् महा-गज इव ॥३॥
entries.literal_english: They recount His amazing deeds: although seven years old, He stood holding the mountain. The comparison is to a great elephant holding a lotus.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: महौजसो महा-बलायाः तनोर् वय आयुर् यौवनं वा कालेन यथा पीयते, तद्वत् । कथम् इत्य् अनुवर्तते ॥४॥
entries.literal_english: The strength of a powerful body is consumed by time as age and life pass; the commentary continues by asking how this could have occurred in Kṛṣṇa’s case.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: अनसोऽधः शयानस्य । मास्यस्य मासास् त्रयः परिच्छेदका यस्य । उदग् ऊर्ध्वं चरणौ हिन्वतश् चालयतः । प्रपदेन पादाग्रेण हतं विपर्यस्तम् अनः कथम् अपतत् ? ॥५॥
word_for_word: of one who was months old
entries.literal_english: How did the cart fall when Kṛṣṇa, only a few months old, was lying beneath it, moving His feet upward and striking the cart with His toe?
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: यः कृष्णो दैत्येन ह्रियमाणः संस् तं तृणावर्तं दैत्यं कथम् अहन्न् इत्य् अर्थः ॥६॥
entries.literal_english: How did Kṛṣṇa, while being carried away by the demon, kill that demon Tṛṇāvarta? This is the meaning.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: हैयङ्गव-स्तैन्ये नव-नीत-चौर्ये । बाहुभ्यां गच्छन् रिङ्गन्न् इत्य् अर्थः ॥७॥
word_for_word: in the theft of fresh butter
entries.literal_english: This refers to His stealing butter and fresh butter while moving and crawling along on His arms.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: मुखतो हन्तुं कामो यस्य तं बक-वेषम् अरिं बाहुभ्यां मुखतः कथम् अपाटयत् ? ॥८-११॥
entries.literal_english: How did He split the enemy who had taken the form of a crane and desired to kill Him from the front? He split him with His arms; the source block is labeled for verses 8–11.

entries.literal_english: He was the most venomous, possessed of extremely cruel poison, and was the king of serpents.

entries.sanskrit: औत्पत्तिकः स्वाभाविकः कथम् ? इति किं सर्वेषाम् आत्मायं स्याद् इति शङ्का ॥१३॥
entries.literal_english: The doubt is: how could this be innate or natural? Could He be the Self of everyone?

entries.sanskrit: उक्तम् अप्य् अतिविस्मयेन अभिनयेन वदन्ति---क्व सप्त-हायन इति ॥१४॥
entries.literal_english: Although it had already been said, they repeat it with great astonishment and expressive wonder: “How could He be only seven years old?”

entries.sanskrit: प्राक् श्रुतम् एव गर्गाचार्य-वाक्यं तच् चरित-परिशीलनेन निवृत्तासम्भावनस्य नन्दस्य कृष्ण-तत्त्वावबोधकं जातं स इदानीं तेनैव वाक्येन गोपानुपदिशति, श्रूयताम् इति ॥१५.२१॥
word_for_word: for one whose doubts have ceased
entries.literal_english: Garga Ācārya’s earlier words, considered in the light of Kṛṣṇa’s deeds, had removed Nanda’s doubts and revealed Kṛṣṇa’s nature. Nanda now instructs the cowherd men by those same words: “Let them be heard.” The source block is labeled for verses 15–21.

entries.sanskrit: तस्मात् तस्य कर्मसु विस्मयो नास्तीति नन्दस्योक्तिः ॥२२॥
entries.literal_english: Therefore, Nanda says, there should be no wonder at His deeds.

entries.sanskrit: इत्य् अद्धा साक्षान् मां प्रति समादिश्य गर्गे च स्व-गृहं गते सति तदानीं तथा मन्यमानोऽपि इदानीं कृष्णं नारायणस्यांशं मन्ये । अत्र हेतुः, अक्लिष्ट-कारिणम् इति ॥२३.२४॥
entries.literal_english: “After directly instructing me and after Garga had returned to his home, I now consider Kṛṣṇa a portion of Nārāyaṇa, although at that time I thought otherwise. The reason is that He performs difficult deeds without difficulty.” The source block is labeled for verses 23–24.

entries.sanskrit:
गोवर्धनोद्धरणं स-परिकरम् अनुस्मरन् प्रकटितैश्वर्यस्य श्री-कृष्णस्य प्रीतिं प्रार्थयते, देव इति । यज्ञ-विप्लवेन या रुट् तया देवे इन्द्रे वर्षति सति । वज्राश्म-पर्षानिलैर् अशनि-जल-शर्करातीव्र-वायुभिः सीदत् पाल-पशु-स्त्रिय आत्म-शरणं सीदन्तः पालाः पशवः स्त्रियश् च यस्मिंस् तत् तथा, आत्मा स्वयम् एव शरणं यस्य तद् गोष्ठं दृष्ट्वा अनुकम्पी उत्स्मयन् हसन् प्रौढिम् आविष्कुर्वन् शैलम् उत्पाट्याबलो बालो लीलार्थम् उच्छिलीन्ध्रं यथा तथैकेन करेण बिभ्रहधद् गोष्ठम् अपात् पालितवान् । एवं महेन्द्र-मद-भित् गवाम् इन्द्र इत्य् उत्तराध्यायार्थं च स्मरति । स एवं-भूतः श्री-कृष्णो नः प्रीयात् प्रीयताम् इति । "षाड्-विंशे दशमे व्यक्तः षड्-विंशो दशमो हरिः । व्यन्क्तु पञ्च-विंशं मां चतुर्-विंशतितः पृथक्"

: वर्षानिलैः
word_for_word: of Him whose opulence was revealed
entries.literal_english: Remembering the lifting of Govardhana together with all its retinue, he prays for favor from Kṛṣṇa, whose opulence was revealed. When Indra rained after the sacrifice was disrupted—with thunderbolts, hailstones and fierce winds—the cowherds, animals and women suffered. Kṛṣṇa, compassionate and smiling as He displayed His majesty, uprooted the mountain and held it with one hand like a mushroom or umbrella, protecting Gokula. The commentary also anticipates the next chapter’s meaning: Kṛṣṇa broke Mahendra’s pride, the true Indra of the cows. May that Kṛṣṇa be pleased with us.
